vt11_papal_loans.topic: Rothschild and Torlonia loans to the Papal States, 1831-1850s; the exclusivity clause; Vigny and the trope

claims.text: Wikipedia: the 1832 loan to the Holy See under Gregory XVI was £400,000; Alessandro Torlonia negotiated for the Holy See and reached terms with James Mayer de Rothschild (Paris); agreement signed 30 November 1831, effective 1832; Carl Mayer von Rothschild (Naples) met the Pope in January 1832 and received the insignia of the (Constantinian) Order of Saint George; a later passage calls it the original 5% contract signed by Rothschild and Torlonia.

Wikipedia attributes the preference clause (Holy See to inform the Rothschilds before approaching another firm, preference on equal terms) to Balla (1913), pp. 228-229, and ties it to Carl von Rothschild's visit to Rome after the 1834 dispute.

1834: Cardinal Antonio Tosti, papal treasurer from July 1834, sought to refinance on better terms; Rothschild opposed early refinancing (Felisini 2017, pp. 109-110); Tosti approached rival Paris banks; the sides reconciled and jointly took the new loan (Wikipedia).

Wikipedia quotes Alfred de Vigny's remark that 'a Jew now reigns over the Pope' among Catholic and other critics (Ludwig Börne; G. G. Belli's sonnet faulting the Pope as much as the bankers); a second loan was made in the early 1850s under Pius IX after the fall of the Roman Republic.

Wikipedia (citing Posner 2015, p. 15): Metternich acted as intermediary for requests to improve conditions for the Jews of the Papal States, incl. Ancona (extra taxes, ghetto property restrictions, professional bans, court evidence rules).

Wikipedia (Carl Mayer von Rothschild): reports that he was permitted to kiss the Pope's hand rather than his foot caused controversy in the Catholic world that the Pope was selling Rome to 'a Jew'; Vatican listed among Naples clients.

Jewish Encyclopedia (1906) loan table lists 'Papal States' 1831: 16,000,000 (francs) and 1845: 2,160,000; text: after the 1834 Sardinian loan went to a rival syndicate, the Rothschilds' 'bearing' policy meant 'the next papal loan was financed by them'; Karl described as banker to the Papal States among others; Union Générale passage ends that 'at the present time the latter are the guardians of the papal treasure' (no source or detail given).

Felisini (2016) abstract: Alessandro Torlonia became the Pope's banker; the 1831 uprisings in the northern provinces strained the papal budget; Torlonia partnered with James de Rothschild in public-debt management; the first Rothschild-Torlonia loan was controversial for its terms and because Rothschild was a Jewish banker.
Felisini's book used the archives of the Rothschild bank in Paris (Tor Vergata record).

Catholic Encyclopedia: Austrian troops withdrew 15 July 1831; by December much of the Papal States was again in revolt; Cardinal Albani appealed to Radetzky; Austrians took Bologna; France seized Ancona in protest and stayed until the Austrians left in 1838.

Hayes on Pollard (2005): Cardinal Antonelli's budget reforms depended on borrowing from the Rothschild house; many saw it as unseemly; Nogara was the first non-Roman to control Vatican finances; Lateran Pacts a windfall.
Balla, The Romance of the Rothschilds, London: E. Nash, 1913 (catalogue).
Union Générale collapsed January 1882 (shares 3,040 to 800 francs, 5-14 Jan); its founder blamed 'Jewish-German banks and Freemasons'; no such conspiracy is now accepted.
Drumont's La France juive (1886, Flammarion, 2 vols, 140 printings in two years) blamed the Union Générale crash on the Rothschild family.
Jewish Virtual Library: Rome's Jews lived in the ghetto for almost 300 years; in 1870 under Victor Emmanuel the ghettos were dismantled and Jews given full citizenship.

claims.text: 1990 chirograph preamble: Leo XIII set up a Commissione ad pias causas in 1887; the Amministrazione per le Opere di Religione got a statute on 17 March 1941; Pius XII's chirograph of 27 June 1942 created the IOR with legal personality, absorbing it; 1944 chirograph; 1990 structure: Commission of five Cardinals, Prelate, Board of Superintendence (five lay members, five-year terms), Direction, three auditors.

Sindona: friend of Montini (Paul VI) from the early 1960s; association with the Vatican Bank from 1969; Franklin National insolvent 8 October 1974; US conviction 1980 (65 counts, 25 years); Italy 1985 fraudulent bankruptcy; life sentence 18 March 1986 for instigating the 1979 Ambrosoli murder; died 22 March 1986 after cyanide in Voghera prison. The article does not mention Rothschild.

De Franssu: CDC 1987; Invesco France 1990; CEO Invesco Europe 1997-2011; EFAMA president 2009-2011; member of the pontifical commission on economic-administrative structures (COSEA) March-September 2014; chairman of the IOR board from 9 July 2014; La Française supervisory board 2015. No Rothschild connection mentioned.
Vatican Press Office announced on 9 July 2014 de Franssu's appointment as IOR president with a new lay board (incl. Mary Ann Glendon, Sir Michael Hintze, Clemens Boersig).

vt11_pauly_2026.topic: François Pauly at the IOR (2026); the Paris PNF inquiry (Aidan)

claims.text: IOR announced 25 March 2026 that François Pauly would be the next President of the Board of Superintendence, succeeding Jean-Baptiste Douville de Franssu, who stays until the Board meeting of 28 April 2026 approving the accounts to 31 December 2025; a succession process over twelve months by the Board and the Commission of Cardinals; the Commission to appoint a new Board member in de Franssu's place subject to ASIF approval. CV as given by the IOR: Luxembourg citizen; banking from late 1980s; Deputy CEO Dexia Crediop Italy 2002-2003; CEO and Chairman of BIL 2011-2016; Vatican Pension Fund board 2017-2021; chairman of La Luxembourgeoise; Economic Affairs Commission of the Archdiocese of Luxembourg. The announcement as reported does not mention Edmond de Rothschild.

Paperjam: Board proposed Pauly in December 2025; the Commission of Cardinals approved on 28 January 2026; de Franssu in post since 2014; Cardinal Giuseppe Petrocchi (president of the Commission) praised de Franssu's 'essential contribution'; de Franssu spoke of a 'profound structural transformation' since 2014.

UBP: Pauly elected to UBP's board in 2024; 35 years in finance, mostly private banking; Dexia, then executive and board member at Sal. Oppenheim and BIL; 'most recently ... CEO of Banque Edmond de Rothschild'; as at 31 Dec 2024 chairman of Compagnie Financière La Luxembourgeoise, board of Cobepa and Tikehau Capital, member of the Board of Superintendence of IOR.

Option Finance, 7 June 2021: Pauly named 'CEO du Groupe' Edmond de Rothschild; director of Edmond de Rothschild (Suisse) and its Luxembourg subsidiary since 2016; vice-chair of Edmond de Rothschild (Europe); chair of the audit and risk committee of Edmond de Rothschild (Suisse) since 2016.

InfoVaticana: CEO and chair of the executive committee of Edmond de Rothschild (Suisse) from June 2021, after Benjamin de Rothschild's death; departure formalized March 2023 (adviser role); Edmond de Rothschild is distinct from Rothschild & Co; the outlet makes no claim of Rothschild influence on Vatican decisions; headline 'groupe Rothschild' broader than body.

Vatican News, 11 May 2026: IOR 2025 net profit €51m (+55.5%), dividend to the Pope €24.3m, client assets €5.9bn, net assets €815.3m, Tier 1 71.9%; de Franssu concluded his term with approval of the 2025 statements; Pauly has taken office as President.

PNF release of 24 March 2026 (Pascal Prache): searches on Friday 20 March 2026 at several places incl. the Paris head office of Edmond de Rothschild (France), 8th arr.; preliminary inquiry opened 17 February 2026 for 'corruption passive d'agent public étranger et complicité de ce délit', entrusted to OCLCIFF; following a signalement by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on 16 February 2026 after the 'Epstein Files' revelations; Paris prosecutor relinquished to PNF; inquiry 'visant notamment' Fabrice Aidan; no role stated; no custody or charge mentioned; no mention of the Vatican or the IOR.
Reuters, 24 March 2026: Aidan has denied wrongdoing; the bank declined to comment; a source said it is co-operating fully.
